summary: Abandoned but not Forgotten turns the stories of twelve NASA machines left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space into an offline, photo-led audio tour. Each machine speaks in the first person at three reading ages (7 to 9, 10 to 13, 14 to 18). Children hear about the missions that went quiet, not only the ones still running. Every story is written from a registry of 47 facts tied to 26 sources. A validator with nine automated checks fails the build if a claim has no citation or a reading level is wrong. The app has captions, keyboard control and reduced motion, and runs from a USB stick with no internet, reaching people the web left out.
details:
• What it does: A tour of 12 machines, each with its own voice, a captioned line-by-line story and a photo. All three reading levels carry the same verified facts.
  • How it works: Facts go into registry.json first, each tied to a source. Stories are written from the registry. Nine automated checks cover sourcing, date precision, band difficulty, cross-contamination, headline numbers, quote provenance, media coverage, voice profiles and DOM integrity. The first draft failed with nine reading-level inversions, two orphan sources and an InSight story that blamed the wrong mission, and we fixed all of them.
  • Impact: It targets 2.6 billion people offline (ITU 2024), 1.3 billion living with a disability (WHO) and 763 million adults with low literacy (UNESCO). We did not add these groups together, because they overlap.
  • Tools: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one offline folder with no install, login or tracking. Fonts are Michroma and Atkinson Hyperlegible. The pitch is a 16:9 HTML deck recorded to video.
  • Creativity: The machines tell their own stories, and the build is gated by citations and reading-level checks, which storytelling projects rarely have.
  • Factors considered: Accessibility, offline reach, factual accuracy and age-appropriate language.
